q: 1. The sand is mixed with lime mortar to ............
explain: Sand acts as an inert filler in lime mortar to prevent excessive shrinkage and the resulting cracks during the setting process.

q: 2. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between ............
explain: Standard consistency is achieved when the Vicat plunger penetrates the paste to a point 5 to 7 mm from the bottom of the mold (which corresponds to 33-35 mm penetration from the top).

q: 3. High alumina cement is produced by fusing together a mixture of ............
options: limestone, gypsum, bauxite, clay and chalk
explain: High Alumina Cement (HAC) is manufactured by fusing a mixture of limestone (calcareous) and bauxite (aluminous) at very high temperatures.

q: 4. Portland cement manufactured from pure white chalk and clay but free form iron-oxide, is known as ............
explain: Iron oxide gives cement its grey colour. White cement is made by using materials free from iron and manganese oxides.

q: 5. The constituent of cement which is responsible for all the undesirable properties of cement is ............
explain: Tri-calcium Aluminate (C3A) generates high heat of hydration, contributes to sulphate attack susceptibility, and can cause flash setting.

q: 6. The cementing property in cement is mainly due to ............
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) is the principal constituent that provides binding strength and determines the quality of the cement.

q: 7. The practical limit of moisture content achieved in air drying of timber is ............
explain: Air seasoning can generally reduce moisture content to about 12-15%, depending on the humidity of the environment.

q: 8. Seasoning is ............
explain: Seasoning of timber is the controlled process of reducing the moisture (sap) content to improve durability and stability.

q: 9. The maximum water-cement ratio for durable concrete is
explain: As Per Key D is answer But While lower ratios are better for strength, a ratio of 0.6 is typically considered the upper limit for ensuring durability and workability in general concrete work.

q: 10. Whitworth compressed steel is obtained when molten steel is subjected to a pressure of
explain: Whitworth steel is produced by subjecting molten steel to a high pressure of approximately $9	ext{ kg/mm}^2$ to eliminate gas bubbles and improve density.

q: 11. If the furnace is provided with insufficient fuel at low temperatures, the type of pig iron Produced, is called
explain: Lower temperatures cause the carbon to remain chemically combined as iron carbide ($Fe_3C$), resulting in hard, brittle White Pig Iron.

q: 12. The asbestos content in asbestos cement sheets is roughly about ...............
explain: Standard asbestos cement sheets usually contain roughly 15% asbestos fibers to provide tensile strength to the brittle cement matrix.

q: 13. Bullet proof glass is made of thick glass sheet sandwiched by a layer of ...............
explain: The 'sandwich' layer is usually polycarbonate or another high-strength thermoplastic that provides the elasticity needed to absorb kinetic energy.

q: 14. Cast steel is manufactured by ...............
explain: Cast steel is produced primarily through the crucible or electric furnace processes to ensure high purity and control over carbon content.

q: 15. The main constituents which imparts hydraulicity to hydraulic lime is ...............
explain: The clay content (silica and alumina) in hydraulic lime reacts with the lime to allow it to set in the absence of air (underwater).

q: 16. The property by virtue of which lime sets under water, is known as ...............
explain: Hydraulicity is the ability of lime (due to its clay/silica content) to set and harden in damp conditions or even under water where air circulation is absent.

q: 17. The normal curing period for lime mortar, is ...............
explain: While lime sets slower than cement, it requires moisture for the carbonation process; a standard initial curing period of 7 days is typically recommended.

q: 18. Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the ...............
explain: Vicat's apparatus with different attachments (plunger, needle, needle with collar) is used to find consistency, initial set, and final set.

q: 19. The expansion of cement should not exceed ............... for any type of Portland cement.
explain: According to IS codes, the expansion of cement measured by the Le-Chatelier apparatus should not exceed 10 mm.

q: 20. The normal consistency of Portland cement is about ...............
explain: Normal consistency (P) is the percentage of water required to produce a paste that allows the Vicat plunger to penetrate 33-35mm; it is usually around 25-30%.

q: 21. The rate of hydration and hydrolysis of cement depends upon its ...............
explain: Finer particles provide more surface area for chemical reactions with water, thus increasing the rate of hydration.

q: 22. The lime which has high calcium oxide content and which sets only in the presence carbon dioxide is called ............
explain: Fat lime (Rich lime) contains high CaO. It hardens slowly through 'carbonation' by absorbing CO2 from the atmosphere.

q: 23. The process of adding water to lime to convert it into a hydrated lime is termed as ............
explain: Slaking is the chemical reaction where quick lime (CaO) reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2].

q: 24. For construction of structures under water, the type of lime used, is .............
explain: Hydraulic lime contains silica and alumina, which allow it to set and harden under water by chemical reaction (hydration) rather than by carbonation from the air.

q: 25. The disease of dry rot in timber is caused by ............
explain: Dry rot is a fungal decay caused by certain fungi that thrive in damp, unventilated conditions where they convert wood into dry, powdery mass.

q: 26. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at considerable depth from earth's surface are called ............
explain: Plutonic rocks (like granite) form deep within the crust where slow cooling leads to large mineral crystals.

q: 27. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plastering is ............
explain: As per Key of book For internal plastering on brick walls, a 1:5 mortar mix is typically recommended for a balance of workability and strength.

q: 28. Brittleness of cold is due to an excess of ............
explain: Excess phosphorus in steel or iron causes 'cold shortness,' making the metal brittle and liable to crack when cold worked.

q: 29. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is ............
explain: Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A) is the most reactive compound and is responsible for the flash set of cement if gypsum is not present.
